transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s work. I’m a barber, and I’ve been doing almost anything to avoid using the straight razor. Switching clients, saying I can’t find the blade, hiding it in the drawer… stuff like that. And if I can’t get out of it, I’m shaking through the whole shave.
Can you describe how you feel when you have to use the straight razor? Is it more of a general discomfort or more like intense fear or anxiety?

It’s more than discomfort. I know it’s just a tool, and I was trained to use it… I can use clippers all day with no problem. But when the straight razor is open there at my station, I get this feeling like I’m about to badly cut myself or hurt the person in the chair.
Do you find yourself avoiding other things besides the straight razor, like certain tools or situations at work, even if they aren’t dangerous?

Mostly it’s the straight razor. I… I’ll go pretty far to not use it—swap clients, say I can’t find a blade, even stick it in a drawer. If I can’t avoid it, I just kind of shake my way through the shave.
Outside of work and the straight razor, do you find yourself feeling anxious or fearful in other situations, like social interactions, public places, or other tasks?
Not really… I mean, nothing that stands out. It’s pretty much just that razor situation.
Has this fear of using the straight razor caused you any significant problems, like trouble sleeping, feeling really upset, or affecting your job performance or relationships?

Yeah… it’s caused problems at work. I’ve lost tips, and a few regulars have complained because I keep avoiding razor shaves or handing them off to someone else.

I also… backed out of a barber battle because they required razor detailing. That was embarrassing.
Have you ever experienced similar feelings of fear or anxiety in other specific situations, even outside of work, like using other tools or being in certain places?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed it with other tools or places. It’s just… that one thing, as far as I can tell.
When did you first notice this fear of using the straight razor? Has it been ongoing for a long time, or did it start more recently?
It started… maybe around 11 months ago. Around when the shop owner and I started arguing about that straight-razor shave package. It’s been going on since then.
Have you ever felt this kind of fear even when you're just thinking about the straight razor, like when it's not even in front of you or when you're at home?

Yeah… sometimes just thinking about it is enough. I know it’s just a tool, and I trained with it, but when I picture it open at my station, I get this feeling like I’m going to cut myself badly or hurt someone.
Have you ever felt fear or anxiety when seeing someone else use a straight razor, or when handling a similar tool, like a knife or scalpel, even outside of work?

Not really with knives or anything like that. It’s mostly the straight razor… when it’s open at my station. I know I’m trained to use it, and clippers are fine, but with that razor I get this feeling like I’m going to cut myself badly or hurt someone.
